resource.name: aws_efs_file_system
resource.description: Provides an Elastic File System (EFS) File System resource.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_efs_file_system` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of scalable, fully-managed Elastic File System (EFS) instances for shared, cloud-native storage in AWS. It is commonly used for scenarios requiring persistent, high-availability storage accessible across multiple EC2 instances, containers, or serverless applications. Users can configure key features such as performance modes (general purpose or max I/O), encryption at rest, lifecycle policies for automatic file system cleanup, and integration with VPCs for secure access.

examples.title: EFS File System w/ tags
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an AWS EFS file system with a custom `creation_token` and apply tags for resource identification. It illustrates the use of the `tags` block to assign metadata, such as a `Name` tag, for easier management and organization of the file system.

examples.title: Using lifecycle policy
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an AWS EFS file system with a lifecycle policy using the `lifecycle_policy` block to automatically transition files to the Infrequent Access (IA) storage class after 30 days. It highlights the use of the `transition_to_ia` argument for cost optimization by managing storage tiers.

arguments.name: availability_zone_name
arguments.description: (Optional) the AWS Availability Zone in which to create the file system. Used to create a file system that uses One Zone storage classes. See user guide for more information.
arguments.llm_summary: The `availability_zone_name` argument for the `aws_efs_file_system` resource allows users to specify the AWS Availability Zone where the file system will be created, enabling the use of One Zone storage classes for cost-optimized, single-AZ deployments. By setting this argument, users can control the geographic placement and redundancy level of the file system to align with specific application requirements or budget constraints.

arguments.name: creation_token
arguments.description: (Optional) A unique name (a maximum of 64 characters are allowed) used as reference when creating the Elastic File System to ensure idempotent file system creation. By default generated by Terraform. See Elastic File System user guide for more information.
arguments.llm_summary: The `creation_token` argument for the `aws_efs_file_system` resource allows users to specify a unique identifier to ensure idempotent creation of an Elastic File System (EFS). By defining this token, users can prevent accidental duplication of file systems during provisioning, aligning with common goals of resource consistency and predictable infrastructure behavior.

arguments.name: encrypted
arguments.description: (Optional) If true, the disk will be encrypted.
arguments.llm_summary: The `encrypted` argument for the `aws_efs_file_system` resource allows users to specify whether the file system should be encrypted at rest, enhancing data security by enabling server-side encryption using AWS-managed keys. Setting this argument to `true` is ideal for meeting compliance requirements or protecting sensitive data stored in the EFS file system.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_efs_file_system` resource represents the unique identifier of the EFS file system. While not required, it is typically used to reference an existing file system for data retrieval or dependency management, enabling users to integrate the resource into workflows or configurations without creating a new file system.

arguments.name: kms_key_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The ARN for the KMS encryption key. When specifying kms_key_id, encrypted needs to be set to true.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kms_key_id` argument allows users to specify the ARN of a KMS encryption key to enable server-side encryption for the Amazon EFS file system. By setting this argument (along with `encrypted = true`), users can control the encryption behavior of the file system, ensuring data at rest is protected using a custom-managed KMS key, which is often aligned with security and compliance requirements.

arguments.name: performance_mode
arguments.description: (Optional) The file system performance mode. Can be either `"generalPurpose"` or `"maxIO"` (Default: `"generalPurpose"`).
arguments.llm_summary: The `performance_mode` argument for the `aws_efs_file_system` resource allows users to specify the file system's performance configuration, choosing between `generalPurpose` for lower latency and `maxIO` for higher throughput in highly parallelized workloads. This setting impacts the EFS's behavior to optimize for either typical application performance or large-scale data processing, aligning with user goals like workload-specific tuning and resource efficiency.

arguments.name: provisioned_throughput_in_mibps
arguments.description: (Optional) The throughput, measured in MiB/s, that you want to provision for the file system. Only applicable with `throughput_mode` set to `provisioned`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `provisioned_throughput_in_mibps` argument allows users to define the desired throughput capacity (in MiB/s) for an Amazon EFS file system when using the `provisioned` throughput mode. This configuration ensures predictable performance by explicitly setting the file system's throughput, making it ideal for workloads requiring consistent and high I/O rates independent of storage size.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) A map of tags to assign to the file system. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_efs_file_system` resource allows users to assign key-value metadata to the file system, enabling organization, categorization, and identification of resources for purposes such as cost allocation, environment labeling, or automation workflows. When set, it overrides provider-level default tags with matching keys, ensuring granular control over resource tagging.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_efs_file_system` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are applied to the file system, including inherited tags from the provider-level configuration. This enables consistent resource tagging for purposes such as cost allocation, environment identification, or organizational compliance, ensuring the file system is easily categorized and managed within broader cloud infrastructure workflows.

arguments.name: throughput_mode
arguments.description: (Optional) Throughput mode for the file system. Defaults to `bursting`. Valid values: `bursting`, `provisioned`, or `elastic`. When using `provisioned`, also set `provisioned_throughput_in_mibps`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `throughput_mode` argument for the `aws_efs_file_system` resource allows users to define how the file system's throughput is managed, offering control over performance scaling. By setting this argument to `bursting`, `provisioned`, or `elastic`, users can configure the file system to dynamically adjust throughput based on activity, allocate fixed throughput, or enable automatic scaling, respectively, aligning with workload requirements and optimizing cost or performance.

blocks.name: lifecycle_policy
blocks.description: (Optional) A file system lifecycle policy object. See `lifecycle_policy` block below for details.

arguments.name: transition_to_archive
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates how long it takes to transition files to the archive storage class. Requires transition_to_ia, Elastic Throughput and General Purpose performance mode. Valid values: `AFTER_1_DAY`, `AFTER_7_DAYS`, `AFTER_14_DAYS`, `AFTER_30_DAYS`, `AFTER_60_DAYS`, `AFTER_90_DAYS`, `AFTER_180_DAYS`, `AFTER_270_DAYS`, or `AFTER_365_DAYS`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `transition_to_archive` argument in the `lifecycle_policy` of the `aws_efs_file_system` resource allows users to define the duration after which files are automatically transitioned to the archive storage class, optimizing cost for infrequently accessed data. By configuring this argument, users can implement data retention policies that align with their storage lifecycle needs, ensuring efficient management of file system resources.

arguments.name: transition_to_ia
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates how long it takes to transition files to the IA storage class. Valid values: `AFTER_1_DAY`, `AFTER_7_DAYS`, `AFTER_14_DAYS`, `AFTER_30_DAYS`, `AFTER_60_DAYS`, `AFTER_90_DAYS`, `AFTER_180_DAYS`, `AFTER_270_DAYS`, or `AFTER_365_DAYS`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `transition_to_ia` argument in the `lifecycle_policy` of the `aws_efs_file_system` resource allows users to define the duration after which files are automatically transitioned to the Infrequent Access (IA) storage class based on their age. This configuration helps optimize storage costs by enabling lifecycle management for less frequently accessed data, aligning with common goals of cost efficiency and automated data tiering.

arguments.name: transition_to_primary_storage_class
arguments.description: (Optional) Describes the policy used to transition a file from infequent access storage to primary storage. Valid values: `AFTER_1_ACCESS`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `transition_to_primary_storage_class` argument in the `lifecycle_policy` of the `aws_efs_file_system` resource allows users to define the behavior for transitioning files from infrequent access storage back to primary storage based on access patterns. By specifying a value like `AFTER_1_ACCESS`, users can configure automated file movement to optimize storage costs while ensuring frequently accessed files are readily available in primary storage.

blocks.llm_summary: The `lifecycle_policy` block within the `aws_efs_file_system` resource defines rules for managing the lifecycle of files stored in the EFS file system, such as transitioning files to the Infrequent Access (IA) storage class based on age or access patterns. Configuring this block enables users to optimize storage costs and automate data tiering by specifying retention policies and access-based transitions.

blocks.name: protection
blocks.description: (Optional) A file system protection object. See `protection` block below for details.

arguments.name: replication_overwrite
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates whether replication overwrite protection is enabled. Valid values: `ENABLED` or `DISABLED`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `replication_overwrite` argument for the `aws_efs_file_system` resource allows users to control whether replication overwrite protection is enabled, safeguarding replicated data from being unintentionally overwritten. Setting this argument to `ENABLED` ensures data integrity in replication scenarios, aligning with user goals of maintaining robust disaster recovery and high availability strategies.

blocks.llm_summary: The "protection" configuration block within the `aws_efs_file_system` resource is used to manage file system protection settings, such as enabling safeguards against accidental deletion or unintended modifications. Configuring this block helps users enhance the resilience and security of their EFS file system by defining protective measures that ensure data integrity and operational continuity.

attributes.name: arn
attributes.description: Amazon Resource Name of the file system.

attributes.name: availability_zone_id
attributes.description: The identifier of the Availability Zone in which the file system's One Zone storage classes exist.

attributes.name: dns_name
attributes.description: The DNS name for the filesystem per documented convention.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: The value of the file system's `Name` tag.

attributes.name: number_of_mount_targets
attributes.description: The current number of mount targets that the file system has.

attributes.name: owner_id
attributes.description: The AWS account that created the file system. If the file system was createdby an IAM user, the parent account to which the user belongs is the owner.

attributes.name: size_in_bytes
attributes.description: The latest known metered size (in bytes) of data stored in the file system, the value is not the exact size that the file system was at any point in time. See Size In Bytes.
